text:
Maria P. (sec): Quick question — we're planning to remove cluster-admin from the private-deploy operator role in the next release. Need confirmation on two things before we cut: (1) audit journaling path for air-gapped installs (where do signed logs live?), and (2) attestation proof we can hand to compliance to justify 'isolation guarantees'. Also: how do we handle KMS integration when on-prem sites can't reach our central KMS?

Josh R. (infra): +1 on the change but we need a migration plan. For journaling, current thinking was local append-only journal + periodic push (rsync) to customer-controlled collector when allowed. For totally air-gapped, we can produce signed audit bundles that are verifiable offline. :thinking:

Ken L. (platform): Re: KMS — for air-gapped customers we should support two modes: (A) customer-managed HSM (they provide a wrapping key, we use envelope encryption locally) or (B) a local KMS proxy that accepts sealed keys from our control plane during onboarding and never calls out after initial sync.

Li W. (sec-engineer): For the audit log format proposal: we should use an append-only chain of signed entries (like a lightweight merkle-ish chain) so integrity can be verified even offline. Example idea (very rough):

```
# audit entry layout (pseudo)
{ "ts": 1714129876, "msg": "operator:apply:rolebind update", "prev_hash": "...", "sig": "base64(...)" }
```

Stored in compressed bundles under `/var/log/redwood/audit-bundles/` and exported as `.tar.sig` with the head signature. That way compliance can verify chain continuity without network access.

Tara S. (sec-lead): Agree with Li. Also we need attestation evidence at onboarding: a signed statement that includes the node TPM/SEV quote (when available), image digest, and runtime policy version. For on-prem, ask customers to provide an attestation verifier or accept signed quotes we produce that reference the local KMS-wrapped attestation key. This satisfies the "we ran on approved hardware and image" ask.

Maria P. (sec): Sounds good. Two follow-ups: (A) who owns implementing the chained signed audit exporter? (B) what RBAC delta tests do we run to prove operator still functions without cluster-admin? Need precise test harness so we can include it in the SOC artifact pack.

Josh R. (infra): I can take the RBAC test harness. Plan: run operator workflows in a kube sandbox with rolebinding assertions and a negative-authz suite. Quick protos: `rbac-test --scenario=operator-deploy --expect-no-cluster-admin` and a CI job that fails the build if any privileged verb appears. We'll wire it to `rbac-bot` for daily diffs.

rbac-bot: rbac-lint finished on branch `drop-operator-cluster-admin` — 2 bindings require manual review: `redwood-operator:role-binding-extra` and `metrics-exporter:clusterrole` (see: https://git.internal/rbac/1234).

Ken L. (platform): For the audit exporter — propose a small service `auditchaind` that runs as a sidecar on each control-plane node. Responsibilities: collect audit stream, produce signed chained entries, rotate signing key (kept in customer HSM or wrapped by local KMS), and emit bundle on demand. Minimal API: `POST /bundle?since=...` returns `.tar.sig`.

Li W. (sec-engineer): NetworkPolicy constraints: by default block all egress from control-plane pods except: (1) local KMS proxy endpoint, (2) collector rsync endpoint (if configured), (3) NTP/time sync, (4) internal cluster DNS. Sample NetPolicy snippet for egress allowlist: 

```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: control-plane-egress-restrict
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-control-plane
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.0.0.0/24    # local KMS proxy
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 8443
  - to:
    - namespaceSelector:
        matchLabels:
          name: telemetry
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 873   # rsync
```

Li W. (sec-engineer): Note: include a feature flag so customers can opt into time-limited egress (e.g., allow collector access windows) — some sites only allow scheduled uploads.

Tara S. (sec-lead): For compliance artifacts, record: (1) RBAC test results, (2) signed audit bundle head + chain anchors, (3) attestation quote + key reference, (4) network policy manifest and evidence of enforcement (e.g., conntrack dump or eBPF trace). These four together form the isolation guarantee evidence.

Maria P. (sec): Excellent. Can we make the signed audit chain verifiable by an offline tool we ship? Compliance wants a binary they can run that verifies continuity and signatures.

Ken L. (platform): Yes — `auditchain-verify` CLI would accept `.tar.sig` and the key/certificate and output a short verification report. We'll make output machine-readable (JSON) and human summary.

Josh R. (infra): Implementation plan / owners: Josh -> RBAC harness + rbac-bot integration (ETA 2w). Ken -> auditchaind + verifier CLI prototype (ETA 3w). Li -> NetPolicy templates + egress windowing design (ETA 1w). Tara & Maria -> compliance pack template and acceptance criteria (ETA 1w).

Maria P. (sec): Thanks. Quick blocker: how do we protect the signing key for auditchaind in fully air-gapped installs where customer refuses HSM? We can't keep unwrapped persistent keys.

Tara S. (sec-lead): Short answer: don't. If customer refuses HSM or wrapped keys we must document residual risk and require manual key custody (customer provides key material sealed in a hardware device). We'll include a "high-residual-risk" checkbox in the SOC pack and require signed legal acceptance.

Ken L. (platform): Alternative: ephemeral in-memory keypair that we rotate daily and include a human-offline ceremony to anchor the chain (customer-signed root anchor) — not ideal but better than nothing. Documented as "limited offline attest" mode.

Maria P. (sec): Okay. I'll draft the compliance wording and the SOC checklist entry for key custody. Putting action items onto the security board. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

rbac-bot: scheduled rbac-diff job created for `drop-operator-cluster-admin` — daily at 02:00 UTC.
